name: The Infinity Castle
_: Fan work after Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba (Shueisha, 2016-2020) and ufotable's anime and films. Nothing of theirs is used: every shape is generated by src/infinitycastle/ from the numbers below. The castle has no plan anyone has published and is never the same twice - ufotable say they built around thirty versions of it for a single television shot - so this is one castle of many, and a seed makes another. Its shape follows what the anime and the films show: a hall, bounded, with a tatami floor that runs to the horizon, rooms hanging from the ceiling, and walls of stacked buildings between.
attribution: Fan work. Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is Koyoharu Gotouge's (Shueisha) and ufotable's; nothing of theirs is used.
_hall: In metres. half: from the middle to each wall; ceil: the height of the ceiling over the floor. clusters: houses, galleries, stacks of rooms and stairs to nowhere in the air; floorHouses: the ones standing on the tatami; blocks: pieces of the walls hung free; bridges: right across, wall to wall; spurs: out from a wall and stopping, then stairs; stairways: long straight stairs up the faces of the walls.

ceiling._: the rooms hung from the ceiling: one column of them to a cell this many metres square, in this many of the cells, and none within 'clearing' of Muzan's lab

_places: Where the places are, in metres from the middle of the floor; y is up; yaw is the way a place faces (0 is +z, south; pi/2 is +x, east).

hall.p: Not a pit and not a tower: a hall. A floor of tatami runs away to where the haze takes it, rooms hang from the ceiling like stalactites, and the walls are buildings stacked from one to the other. In between, in the air, rooms and stairs and bridges every way up. From outside, in the film's end credits, the whole of it is one block.
hall.sub: 760 m each way and 520 m high here. The films never give a size; ufotable's director of photography wanted it 'infinite'.

stage.p: A broad deck of polished boards on stilts against the north wall. When Muzan calls the Upper Moons they arrive here, and Nakime watches from the ledge at the back of it, in front of the great doors. A stair runs straight up to it from the floor, flight after flight.

nakime.p: The castle is her Blood Demon Art. She kneels on the ledge in black, the biwa upright in her lap and her hair over her eyes, and when she strikes it the castle moves: rooms slide past each other and turn over, doors open onto falls. Press Biwa to have her play.
nakime.sub: Upper Moon Four by the time of the Infinity Castle arc.

lab.p: In the dark middle of the ceiling, at the bottom of a cone of red lights, a room hangs the wrong way up: a desk, shelves, flasks and tubes and vessels on stands. Muzan works here standing on the ceiling, which is to say on his floor, looking for a way to stand the sun.
lab.sub: Up is local: every room keeps its own.

wayin.p: At the end of the Hashira Training Muzan comes to the Ubuyashiki mansion and the Hashira close on him there; then the floor under them turns to sliding doors, and the doors open. They fall into the castle. Here that floor is in the ceiling, and through the doors the mansion is burning.
wayin.sub: Press Fall to go the way they went: 520 m, to the floor.

floor.p: Where the fall comes down: a floor of polished boards laid on the tatami, a field of it, with lamps on posts round the edge. In the film a crowd of demons is waiting on one like it.

tatami.p: Tatami, mat after mat, a ken by half a ken each, to the horizon: the floor of the castle as the anime shows it, with the rooms of the ceiling hanging over it and the walls lost in the haze.

ceiling.p: Boards, and hung from them, like stalactites, rooms: columns of one to five, each a little under the last, every one the wrong way up and lit through small slatted windows.
ceiling.sub: Some of them are four storeys deep.

cocoon.p: After the mansion, Muzan closes himself inside a cocoon of flesh to break down the drug Tamayo put into him. It fills the middle of a hall, and its roots go out across the tatami and up the fusuma.
cocoon.sub: It pulses. It is not doing it for your benefit.

well.p: Seventy metres of stairs round a square well against the east wall. A place for someone to wait at the top of while someone else climbs: Kaigaku, Upper Moon Six, for Zenitsu. Their fight ends in a fall.
well.sub: Twenty-two flights, turning right at every landing.

doma.p: The one part of the castle lit teal instead of amber: a lake of lotus on the floor, boardwalks across it with lamps on posts, and at the back of it, on stilts, a palace - two towers of five roofs and a hall between them at the top of a red stair. Doma waits in it for whoever comes. His arts are ice and lotus.
doma.sub: Shinobu Kocho finds him here. Later, Kanao and Inosuke.

akaza.p: A floor of dark polished boards against the west wall, open to the castle behind a heavy rail, with lamps along the beams over it. Akaza's Destructive Death: Compass Needle draws a compass under his feet, twelve needles and a snowflake, the shape of the hairpin Koyuki wore, the girl he was to marry; here it is drawn on the boards in light. In front of the hall the castle has thrown up pillars at an angle, with water pouring off them.
akaza.sub: Tanjiro and Giyu fight him here. The fight goes over the edge more than once.

kokushibo.p: A long hall of great round pillars high on the west wall, lit pale grey-green, its walls rooms stacked six high. Kokushibo, Upper Moon One, fights Muichiro, Genya, Sanemi and Gyomei among pillars. His Moon Breathing leaves crescents; there are some cut into the floor.
kokushibo.sub: In the manga. The films have not got here yet.

walls.p: Buildings on buildings from the floor to the ceiling: runs of lit shoji and dark ones, doors open onto nothing, fusuma painted in gold, balustrades with lamps along them, eaves. ufotable's director of photography called it Japanese-esque but not Japanese - a Japan designed by someone who has never seen it - and more like a city than a castle.
walls.sub: Each strum deals the doors again, outward from Nakime at 140 m/s.
